arxiv-2107-10885.title: Laplace and saddlepoint approximations in high dimensions
arxiv-2107-10885.creator: Yanbo Tang, Nancy Reid, Yanbo Tang, Nancy Reid
arxiv-2107-10885.description: Abstract We examine the behaviour of the Laplace and saddlepoint approximations in the high-dimensional setting, where the dimension of the model is allowed to increase with the number of observations. Approximations to the joint density, the marginal posterior density and the conditional density are considered.

arxiv-2207-03150.title: Small Field models with ACTPol and BICEP3 data - Likelihood analysis.
arxiv-2207-03150.creator: and Ram Brustein
arxiv-2207-03150.description: Abstract We perform a Bayesian analysis for small field models of inflation, using the most recent datasets produced by Planck‘18, ACTPol, and BICEP3. We employ Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) to perform analyses with model coefficients, instead of their proxy slow-roll parameters.

arxiv-2308-10839.title: Vision Transformer Pruning Via Matrix Decomposition Conference: ; Transformer Pruning; Matrix Computation
arxiv-2308-10839.creator: Tianyi Sun
arxiv-2308-10839.description: Abstract . This is a further development of Vision Transformer Pruning ( Zhu et al. 2021b ) via matrix decomposition. The purpose of the Vision Transformer Pruning is to prune the dimension of the linear projection of the dataset by learning their associated importance score in order to reduce the storage, run-time memory, and computational demands.

arxiv-2312-14760.title: Action formalism for geometric phases from self-closing quantum trajectories
arxiv-2312-14760.creator: Dominic Shea, Alessandro Romito
arxiv-2312-14760.description: Abstract When subject to measurements, quantum systems evolve along stochastic quantum trajectories that can be naturally equipped with a geometric phase observable via a post-selection in a final projective measurement. When post-selecting the trajectories to form a close loop, the geometric phase undergoes a topological transition driven by the measurement strength.

arxiv-2403-17760.title: Constructions Are So Difficult That Even Large Language Models Get Them Right for the Wrong Reasons
arxiv-2403-17760.description: Abstract In this paper, we make a contribution that can be understood from two perspectives: from an NLP perspective, we introduce a small challenge dataset for NLI with large lexical overlap, which minimises the possibility of models discerning entailment solely based on token distinctions, and show that GPT-4 and Llama 2 fail it with strong bias.

arxiv-2601-22856.title: OptiMAG: Structure-Semantic Alignment via Unbalanced Optimal Transport
arxiv-2601-22856.creator: Yilong Zuo, Xunkai Li, Zhihan Zhang, Qiangqiang Dai, Ronghua Li, Guoren Wang
arxiv-2601-22856.description: Abstract Multimodal Attributed Graphs (MAGs) have been widely adopted for modeling complex systems by integrating multi-modal information, such as text and images, on nodes. However, we identify a discrepancy between the implicit semantic structure induced by different modality embeddings and the explicit graph structure.

pmc-10650755.title: Behavior of Inflatable Drop-Stitch Fabric Panels Subjected to Bending and Compression
pmc-10650755.creator: William G Davids, Haim Abramovich
pmc-10650755.description: In this paper, the mechanics of inflatable drop-stitch panels are investigated, including the impact of large shear deformations, nonlinearity due to wrinkling of the panel skin that occurs under net compressive strain, work done by the confined internal air, and the effect of the drop-stitch yarns on the panel skin stresses.

pmc-10716390.title: Examining the rural–urban differentials in yoga and mindfulness practices among middle-aged and older adults in India: secondary analysis of a national representative survey
pmc-10716390.creator: Umakanta Sahoo, Santosh K Sharma, Harshita Chari, Soumya Ranjan Nayak, Waad Ali, T Muhammad
pmc-10716390.description: Physical activity and mental well-being play an important role in reducing the risk of various diseases and in promoting independence among older adults. Appropriate physical activity, including yoga and mindfulness practices, can help rectify the loss of independence due to aging and have a positive influence on physical health and functional activities.

pmc-11435289.creator: Youzhen Xiang
pmc-11435289.description: ns, including crop health monitoring, disease detection, forest parameter estimation, soil quality assessment, water stress analysis, and nutrient management. These studies not only highlight advances in their respective fields but also reveal the complex interplay between spectral technologies, machine learning, and sustainable resource management in agricultural ecosystems.

pmc-11602906.title: Dicloxacillin is an inducer of intestinal P‐glycoprotein but neither dicloxacillin nor flucloxacillin increases the risk of stroke/systemic embolism in direct oral anticoagulant users
pmc-11602906.creator: Ditte B. Iversen, Ann‐Cathrine Dalgård Dunvald, Martin Thomsen Ernst, Shahab Abtahi, Patrick Souverein, Olaf Klungel, Glenn Brøde Jeppesen, Flemming Nielsen, Kim Brøsen, Helen S. Hammer, Oliver Pötz, Per Damkier, Erkka Järvinen, Anton Pottegård, Tore B. Stage
pmc-11602906.description: AimWe aimed to assess if dicloxacillin/flucloxacillin reduces the therapeutic efficacy of direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and the underlying molecular mechanism.MethodsIn a randomized, crossover study, we assessed whether dicloxacillin reduces oral absorption of drugs through P‐glycoprotein (P‐gp) during 10 and 28 days of treatment.

pmc-11710036.title: Polygenic risk score analysis suggests hypothyroidism as a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11710036.creator: Ignazio Piras, Marcus Naymik, Janith Don, Nicholas J Schork, Don Saner, Matthew J Huentelman
pmc-11710036.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s Disease (AD) is characterized by cognitive decline due to synaptic loss and neuron death, with amyloid‐β plaques and neurofibrillary tau tangles as key pathological hallmarks. Although genetics account for about 70% of AD risk, modifiable factors also significantly contribute to AD and dementia onset and AD‐resilience.

pmc-11812699.title: Documenting capacity and existing gaps in reporting adverse events following immunisation in Northern Ghana: a quantitative cross-sectional survey of healthcare workers
pmc-11812699.creator: Nana Akosua Ansah, Daniel Weibel, Samuel Tomilola Oladokun, Enyonam Duah, Patrick Ansah, Abraham Oduro, Miriam Sturkenboom
pmc-11812699.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundImmunisation remains an indispensable tool in preventing infectious diseases. A robust pharmacovigilance system assures the public of vaccine safety, particularly in countries like Ghana where there is relatively low reporting of adverse events following immunisation (AEFIs).

pmc-12518781.title: Lower Extremity Kinematic and Kinetic Adaptations During a Half Marathon
pmc-12518781.creator: Wenjin Wang, Shulin Xu, Igor Komnik, Josef Viellehner, Jingmin Liu, Wolfgang Potthast
pmc-12518781.description: This study aimed to clarify the biomechanical adaptations recreational runners experience during a half marathon. Thirty‐seven healthy runners completed a half marathon as fast as possible on a laboratory‐instrumented treadmill. Kinematic and kinetic data were collected every 5 km from 0 to 20 km.

However, the rapid proliferation of unverified content on websites targeting the general population raises serious concerns about health misinformation.
